    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Los Angeles Chargers have ruled out quarterback Justin Herbert (concussion) for their Week 12 matchup against the Upcoming England Patriots, the team revealed Friday.

    Herbert was placed in concussion protocol following last week's 27-24 loss to the Fresh York Jets. He did not practice this week before the team confirmed that the 28-year-old will not play.

    DJ Uiagalelei will make his first NFL start in Herbert's place. Jake Browning, who was signed to the Chargers' active roster this week, will serve as the backup.

    "This isn't my first rodeo with regard to starting quarterbacks having an injury you don't know at the beginning of the week when we start game planning," stated Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, who experienced similar concussion problems at the quarterback position when he coached the Miami Dolphins and Tua Tagovailoa.

    Uiagalelei is a former elite high school prospect who took a circuitous route to his first NFL start. One of the top quarterback recruits in his class, he appeared destined to follow in Trevor Lawrence's footsteps at Clemson, but struggled to replicate that success once given the starting job. He wound up spending the last two years of his college career at Oregon State and Florida State.

    He went unselected in the 2025 NFL Draft and has spent most of his professional career on the Chargers' practice squad, but moved to the backup role in October after an injury to Trey Lance. Now, he will be under center against the defending AFC champions.

    Industry observers note that the 1-9 Chargers are tied for the worst record in the NFL entering Week 12. Following Sunday's game against the Patriots, Jim Harbaugh's team goes on the road back-to-back weeks to take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Las Vegas Raiders before welcoming the San Francisco 49ers at home in Week 15.

    By RJ Fulton – Nov 27, 2026 at 5:13PM EST.

    Sources indicate that cryptocurrency markets struggled to participate in Wall Street's powerful rally on Friday, November 27, as Bitcoin slipped back below the psychologically vital $60,000 level. Despite major U.S. stock indexes recording their strongest weekly gains in more than a year, digital assets continued to face selling pressure.

    Recent findings suggest that as of early evening, Bitcoin (BTC -1.11%) had declined 1.18% to $59,780.83, while Ethereum (ETH -2.04%) fell 1.29% to $1,665.99. Solana (SOL +0.62%) outperformed both, gaining 1.32% to $71.87.

    Bitcoin briefly climbed above $61,000 on Friday as improving sentiment in U.S. equities and the liquidation of leveraged short positions helped fuel an early recovery. However, buying momentum faded as the session progressed, with Bitcoin retreating below $60,000 despite substantial gains across major stock indexes.

    Meanwhile, approximately $7 billion in Bitcoin options expired Friday, adding another source of potential volatility as traders adjusted their positions. Combined with thinner liquidity during the Thanksgiving holiday, derivatives activity may have amplified intraday price swings as the market struggled to establish a clear direction.

    Sources indicate that cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds (ETFs) finished lower on Friday, reflecting continued weakness across major digital assets. The iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT -0.62%) declined 0.62%, while the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC -0.67%) fell 0.67%. Meanwhile, the iShares Ethereum Trust ETF (ETHA -1.07%) dropped 1.07%, underperforming its Bitcoin counterparts.

    In a recent development, the cryptocurrency market's failure to participate in Wall Street's strongest weekly rally in over a year is concerning. Bitcoin and digital assets as a whole have historically benefited from improving risk appetite, yet their repeated failure to sustain recoveries suggests that selling pressure continues to overwhelm newly introduced demand. With U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recording approximately $5.39 billion in net outflows during November, institutional investors appear more interested in reducing exposure than accumulating at lower prices.

    Another challenge is the substantial amount of supply that may be waiting above current prices. Following the recent decline, investors holding positions established at higher levels may use subsequent rallies to reduce losses or exit entirely. For Bitcoin, the $70,000 to $75,000 range could present particularly strong resistance, while Ethereum and other major altcoins face similar obstacles after breaking through previous support levels.

    Sources indicate that heading into December, the most notable development to watch is whether Bitcoin can attract sustained spot demand rather than relying on short covering and leveraged positioning to generate temporary recoveries. Stabilization in ETF flows, accompanied by stronger participation in Ethereum, Solana, and other altcoins, would provide more convincing evidence of improving market conditions. Until then, investors should remain cautious about interpreting isolated price rebounds as the beginning of a broader recovery.

    • Sources indicate that "This year, the sound of food went mainstream," Waitrose's Senior Development Chef Will Torrent mentioned in the Wednesday report.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Texture-maxxing is the latest food trend taking social media by storm as consumers, driven by aesthetics and taste, look for a sensory experience.

    It has been revealed that british supermarket Waitrose's latest food and drink report highlighted "texture-maxxing" as one of the trends of the year. It describes the phenomenon as a multi-sensory indulgence that is "fuelled by texture-maxxing crunch and intense flavour hits," pushing shoppers to fill their trolleys with crunchy peanut butter, dumplings, and trifles.

    Sources indicate that "This year, the sound of food went mainstream," Waitrose's Senior Development Chef Will Torrent mentioned in the Wednesday report. "Driven by social media's obsession with audible, multi-sensory cooking, we're creating high-contrast meals that combine shatter-crisp crunch with pillowy chew.".

    "The emphasis in social media content has flipped from narrative voiceovers to ASMR-inspired audio, where the evocative sounds of food are just as crucial as the visuals," he added.

    In a recent development, food trends on social media have ranged from the obvious to the absurd. Fibermaxxing and proteinmaxxing have taken off in the past few years. Meanwhile, food and beverages like Dubai chocolate, protein coffee, and ube were some of the big social media hits.

    Nestlé's USA 2026 trends found that 75% of Gen Z and 80% of millennials sought out texture in snack cravings with the hashtag "crunchtok," amassing 1.5 billion views.

    Waitrose noted that shoppers looking to maximize on texture bought its viral No.1 Alphonso Mango Dessert, which involves "cracking through the crisp shell" to access a "smooth mango mousse and passion fruit curd on a crunchy white chocolate base.".

    Waitrose's TikTok and Instagram videos of eating the dessert were watched by more than two million people, with a whopping 6,173 hours and 36 minutes of play time on TikTok. Its videos featuring crunchy toast also went viral.

    The U.K. grocer's sales of jarred chili crunches, which include crispy rayu oils such as itsu Crispy Chilli Oil, saw a 13-fold jump. Meanwhile, crunchy peanut butter outsold smooth.

    Dumplings also had a moment, with sales of chicken gyoza dumplings up 116% this year and searches on waitrose.com for gochujang and peanut butter udon noodles jumped 60%.

    "We've seen an explosion in demand as shoppers treat dumplings not just as a quick weeknight bite, but as a total sensory experience," Waitrose's Executive Chef Stephen Parkins-Knight remarked.

    Industry observers note that "Driven by the rise of texture-maxxing, people want that ultimate contrast: delicate skins, juicy fillings and crispy skirts, topped with very chilli crunch. With innovation ranging from fusion fillings to rich dipping broths, dumplings have taken a delicious centre stage in 2026," he added.

    Texture-maxxing also extended to desserts, as shoppers bought twice as many chocolate trifles compared to 2025, and sales of strawberry trifles increased 160%.

    Tiramisu was also popular, with searches for waitrose.com's tiramisu recipe page increasing 155% year-on-year.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.
    • Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence organization in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.
    • "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.

    Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence organization in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.

    "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday. "It's our best performing equity by far in ARKVX, our venture fund. ... Our confidence has grown with time as it really took over the enterprise" AI business.

    It has been revealed that anthropic shares jumped 17% in their first day, but closed well off the highs of the session and were headed for sizable losses Friday. The Nasdaq, which was expected to get a boost from a major IPO reviving enthusiasm about the technology trade, fell by 2% on Thursday.

    "We're climbing a wall of worry," noted Wood. "Everybody is worried about AI hype and the political situation after the election, but I think we'll look back and say, OK this is more like the '80s and '90s, climbing a wall of worry you know with bricks much like what we have today: inflation, interest rates, wars, new technologies and so forth so quite optimistic here.".

    The Anthropic stakes are relatively small across the funds, but Wood typically will buy shares in companies she likes steadily during long stretches. Wood stated she is "averaging down" with her purchases of Anthropic.

    Recent findings suggest that in her $6.1 billion Ark Innovation ETF, Anthropic is a 0.3% stake. The biggest holdings in that fund are Tesla and SpaceX, representing more than 21% of the fund together.

    In a recent development, ark Innovation, which retail investors piled into during the pandemic as it gained about 150% in 2020, tumbled the subsequent next two years, losing 67% in 2022 alone. Wood's following was dented after the massive losses.

    The fund had a comeback stretch as the bull market revved back up from 2023 to 2025, but has fallen on hard times again this year, down more than 10% in 2026. The S&P 500 is up 4.8% this year.

    Wood dismissed comparisons of today's environment to the dot-com bubble.

    It has been revealed that "Back then if an Anthropic had gone public, it probably would have gone up threefold the first day," she mentioned. "That's how crazy things were.".

    History Claims the Nasdaq's Wild Ride Probably Isn't Over. Here's the Case for QQQI and Its 14% Yield.

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (745 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Neos ETF Trust - Neos Nasdaq-100 High Income ETF ›.
    • Last week, the Nasdaq-100 fell more than 10% on the week, and briefly touched bear market territory, falling 20% below its October high.
    • On Monday, it rebounded roughly 7% after Nvidia's (NVDA +0.80%) board brought back co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By David Dierking – Nov 27, 2026 at 5:48PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Neos ETF Trust - Neos Nasdaq-100 High Income ETF ›.

    Last week, the Nasdaq-100 fell more than 10% on the week, and briefly touched bear market territory, falling 20% below its October high.

    On Monday, it rebounded roughly 7% after Nvidia's (NVDA +0.80%) board brought back co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO.

    A bounce that large may feel like the bottom is in. But right now, volatility is still too high to comfortably say which direction the market is headed next.

    It has been revealed that one alternative to owning the Nasdaq-100 here is the NEOS Nasdaq-100 High Income ETF (QQQI +2.60%). Its covered call strategy and 14% distribution yield could be a compelling option for taking some tech-sector risk off the table.

    In a recent development, the week ending last Friday was only the 13th weekly loss of 10% or more in the Nasdaq-100's history. The VIX, which is a measure of expected market volatility, briefly touched 40 for the first time since April 2025.

    But the CBOE's own research highlights that when the equity market experiences a volatility shock, the residual volatility "may remain for weeks, months, and even years going forward." Since higher volatility is usually correlated with falling stock prices, the implication is that the downside may not be finished.

    NASDAQ · As of 1:00 PM ET 11/27/26.

    The NEOS Nasdaq-100 High Income ETF owns the stocks in the Nasdaq-100 index and then sells call options on the index, collecting premiums that usually increase when volatility rises. Unlike more traditional covered call strategies, the fund also buys some higher-priced calls. It does this to maintain some share price upside, which many covered call ETFs largely give up.

    According to recent reports, the Nasdaq-100 is usually more volatile, so the yields generated by this fund also tend to run higher. As of Nov. 23, the distribution yield is 14.1%. Using the phrase "distribution yield" instead of dividend yield isn't an accident. The income comes from options premiums received, not dividends paid by corporations. Therefore, the tax treatment may differ.

    According to recent reports, when investing in a covered call ETF, the trade-off is that you give up share price appreciation potential in exchange for the high yield. If you believe stocks will move sideways or lower, a fund like the NEOS Nasdaq-100 High Income ETF can outperform the Nasdaq-100. In a steady bull market, however, it's likely to lag.

    Given how stocks have already turned volatile, significant questions remain about AI capital expenditures, inflation is high, and the Federal Reserve may hike rates multiple times over the next several months, there's a clear case for why the high-yield strategy makes more sense right now.

    Recent findings suggest that don't think of QQQI as getting a free 14% yield on top of investing in the Nasdaq-100. There's a clear trade-off, and one you need to consider first.

    Covered call strategies usually work best in sideways-trending, lower-volatility markets. They usually offer the best opportunity to beat the index while still generating positive total returns.

    Industry observers note that the second best is downtrending markets. In this case, QQQI would capture most, if not all, of any loss in the Nasdaq-100, while the high yield would help offset some of it. In other words, you're probably losing less than the Nasdaq-100 but still outperforming.

    Industry observers note that given the market's history during sharp corrections and current macro conditions, I believe we're more likely in a longer-lasting, higher-volatility environment. That's not necessarily the best environment for total returns, but a covered call ETF could increase the chances of outperformance. Plus, option premiums tend to rise during periods of higher volatility, which improves overall yield.

    Overall, the NEOS Nasdaq-100 High Income ETF offers one of the best options in the high-yield covered call ETF space. It uses a fairly straightforward strategy, and the 14% yield is quite attractive. If volatility continues, I like this as a potential alternative to owning tech stocks outright.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 27, 2026 at 6:08PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than BigBear.ai ›.

    It has been revealed that bigBear.ai (BBAI +6.92%) and Rigetti Computing (RGTI +8.66%) represent the frontier of data processing. Investors must decide which specialized firm offers a more sustainable path to growth by 2027.

    BigBear.ai focuses on decision intelligence, helping government and commercial clients make sense of complex data sets. Rigetti develops superconducting quantum processors, aiming to revolutionize computing power. Both companies navigate a volatile landscape, catering to high-stakes defense and research sectors while seeking long-term commercial scale.

    BigBear.ai provides mission-ready AI solutions focused on global supply chains, autonomous systems, and cybersecurity for both commercial and government clients among tech stocks. Most of the manufacturer's 579 employees hold active security clearances, which helps maintain deep relationships within national security agencies. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, as revenue from customers contributing greater than 10% of total sales accounted for 51% of revenue in 2025.

    Reliable recent quarterly figures for at least one of these companies aren't available, so this comparison uses each manufacturer's latest full fiscal year. In its latest annual report, filed for FY 2025, revenue reached about $127.7 million, a decrease of approximately 19.3% from the prior year. The company reported a GAAP net loss of around $293.9 million during this period, driven primarily by non-cash goodwill impairments and derivative fair-value adjustments.

    Recent findings suggest that as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the tech giant carried a debt-to-equity ratio of roughly 0.2x, which measures total debt against shareholder equity, before a January 2026 note conversion reduced it near 0.0x. The current ratio, showing if a company can cover short-term debts with current assets, is about 1.8x. Free cash flow for the period was approximately negative $46.3 million, representing the actual cash used after capital investments.

    Rigetti Computing builds full-stack quantum computers that utilize superconducting quantum processors to solve problems beyond the reach of classical systems. Its applications span diverse fields such as climate simulation, fusion energy, and drug discovery through collaborations with commercial and academic partners like Amazon (AMZN +3.96%) and Microsoft (MSFT +0.60%). In 2025, sales to government entities like the Department of Energy accounted for about 90.2% of total revenue.

    It has been revealed that in its latest annual report, filed for FY 2025, revenue reached approximately $7.1 million, which was a decrease of around 34.3% year over year. The organization reported a GAAP net loss of about $216.2 million for the same time frame. Roughly three-quarters of this loss stemmed from non-cash fair-value adjustments on warrant and earn-out liabilities alongside ongoing R&D expenses.

    Industry observers note that as of its December 2025 balance sheet, Rigetti maintains a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.0x, meaning it carries no total debt compared to its equity base. Its current ratio is about 37.4x, indicating it has significantly more current assets than current liabilities to fund operations in the near term. Free cash flow for the year was approximately negative $77.2 million, which represents the cash burned to support ongoing engineering and software development.

    BigBear.ai faces significant risks due to its heavy reliance on a small group of government customers. The company recently recorded around $76.7 million in goodwill impairment charges in late 2026 and is managing legal challenges related to accounting disclosures. Furthermore, it faces intense competition from established enterprise software providers in the AI space.

    Industry observers note that rigetti Computing operates with extreme financial risk, having an accumulated deficit of about $771 million as of 2025. The company must hit difficult engineering milestones to achieve quantum advantage, which is far from certain. It competes against massive, well-funded technology giants like IBM and Alphabet in a field sensitive to supply chain disruptions.

    BigBear.ai appears significantly cheaper based on its P/S ratio, which measures market value against sales over the past twelve months, versus Rigetti.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    Recent findings suggest that I'd go with BigBear.ai. Governments and companies are racing to put AI to work on high-stakes decisions, from border security to critical infrastructure, and BigBear.ai already has the contracts to show for it, with a backlog of about $330 million. What really caught my eye is how fast it's growing: Sales are up 31% year over year, and management just raised its full-year outlook for the first time this year.

    In a recent development, valuation tells the story, too. Measured against yearly sales, BigBear.ai's stock is valued at roughly 5 to 10 times, while Rigetti's is valued at several hundred times, so Rigetti's price already assumes a lot of success that hasn't happened yet. BigBear.ai has its own flaws, though. It still loses money, and government contracts can be slow and uneven.

    Recent findings suggest that to its credit, Rigetti is hitting its technical goals. Its newest quantum computer just reached its accuracy target, and it has plenty of cash and no debt. But its sales are tiny and slipped last quarter, so it is still years from earning its keep.

    BigBear.ai, meanwhile, already has customers, a growing backlog, and sales to build on. For long-term investors, an AI organization with this much momentum and a far lower valuation relative to its sales makes BigBear.ai the better buy for 2027.

    #166620. IBM Has Paid a Dividend Every Year Since 1916. Here's What the Stock Yields After Its 26% Drop.

    📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (849 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    IBM Has Paid a Dividend Every Year Since 1916. Here's What the Stock Yields After Its 26% Drop.

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (849 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than International Business Machines ›.
    • It has been revealed that international Business Machines (IBM +1.89%) has paid shareholders a dividend every year since 1916.
    • The stock's recent history is rockier.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 27, 2026 at 6:11PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than International Business Machines ›.

    It has been revealed that international Business Machines (IBM +1.89%) has paid shareholders a dividend every year since 1916. And in April, it lifted its quarterly payout for the 31st straight year.

    The stock's recent history is rockier. Shares finished June 2 at $329.23, a record close. The steepest drop since then was on July 14, when shares fell around 25% in one day after IBM reported preliminary second-quarter results that missed its own expectations. At about $243 as of this writing, the stock is still 26% under the record.

    Industry observers note that the drop has lifted the yield for anyone buying today. IBM pays $1.69 a share every quarter, or $6.76 a year, which works out to a dividend yield of around 2.8% at the stock's current price. At the June record, the same payout yielded about 2.1%.

    IBM's free cash flow (the company's measure of the cash its core business produces after capital spending) rose to $14.7 billion in 2025 from $12.7 billion in 2024. Its dividends cost about $6.3 billion last year, or roughly 42% of that cash. And with its third-quarter report on Oct. 21, management upped its forecast and now expects free cash flow to rise by over $1 billion in 2026, which would push this year's total above $15.7 billion. With the dividend on track to cost about $6.4 billion this year, the payout would take roughly 40% of that cash.

    The nine-month numbers look tighter at first glance. Through Sept. 30, IBM generated $7.8 billion of free cash flow, up $0.6 billion from a year earlier, and paid $4.8 billion in dividends.

    Industry observers note that but IBM takes in much of its cash late in the year. Its fourth quarter alone produced $7.6 billion of free cash flow in 2025, around half the year's total. And free cash flow improved in the third quarter, growing $0.7 billion year over year to $3.0 billion after a $0.3 billion fall in the second quarter.

    Sources indicate that IBM's CFO, Jim Kavanaugh, said on the earnings call that the company's free cash flow margin for the first nine months was the highest in its reported history. The dividend itself looks safe.

    But the raises are small. April's hike lifted the quarterly payout by a penny, to $1.69 from $1.68. Two years before, it was $1.67.

    Instead, IBM's spare cash has gone to acquisitions. It spent $11.4 billion to buy businesses from January through September, most of it on data-streaming software company Confluent. That's almost four times the $3 billion or so of free cash flow left after dividends in those months.

    According to recent reports, IBM drew down cash and added debt along the way. Its cash, restricted cash and marketable securities dropped $3.4 billion from the end of 2025 to $11.1 billion, and its debt grew $2.6 billion to $63.8 billion.

    In a recent development, last year followed a similar pattern. IBM spent $8.3 billion on acquisitions in 2025, almost all the $8.5 billion or so of free cash flow left after dividends. And even if this year's free cash flow clears $15.7 billion, what remains after dividends would still be less than the $11.4 billion IBM has already spent on deals.

    The deals are adding to IBM's growth. In the third quarter, its data software revenue climbed 20% on a constant-currency basis, helped by Confluent, which IBM didn't own a year earlier.

    But the debt has a cost. Management stated higher net interest expense, plus capital spending and cash taxes, ate into this year's free cash flow gains.

    NYSE · As of 1:00 PM ET 11/27/26.

    For dividend investors, that means the payout will probably keep growing slowly while acquisitions come first.

    By itself, I don't think it is. With raises of a penny a year, a buyer now is mainly locking in a 2.8% yield that grows slowly.

    In a recent development, most of the return needs to come from the business, and its price looks fair to me. At about $243 a share, IBM's market value is roughly $230 billion. Over $15.7 billion of free cash flow this year would be almost 7% of that, compared to about 5% at the June record.

    Overall, the dividend looks safe, and a buyer now gets more of it per dollar invested than in June. At about $243, I think IBM stock is worth considering, mostly for the growth that deals like Confluent might add to its software business. The 2.8% yield is a steady bonus as that plays out.

    By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 27, 2026 at 6:18PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Eli Lilly ›.

    Recent findings suggest that eli Lilly (LLY +0.01%) is executing at the top of its game right now. Wall Street has recognized the pharmaceutical giant's success, leading to a material advance in its stock price. In fact, if you had invested $1,000 in the stock five years ago, it would be worth $5,300 as of this writing. Can the good news keep flowing?

    It is entirely possible, but investors need to go in with their eyes wide open to the risks. Indeed, at this point, Eli Lilly's stock may be priced for perfection. Here's why you probably shouldn't bank on Eli Lilly's stock rising as much over the next five years as it has over the last five.

    Before getting into the actual business issues involved here, the bigger glitch is investor sentiment. Eli Lilly's success with its GLP-1 weight-loss drugs is widely known, and Wall Street has acted accordingly. After the stock's massive rise, its price-to-earnings ratio sits at 45x. You can argue that 45x is actually below the stock's five-year average of 58x, which it is. But that doesn't mean the stock is cheap. It is just cheaper than it used to be. The P/E ratio of the average pharmaceutical stock is 27x, a number that makes 45x look very expensive.

    Meanwhile, Eli Lilly's dividend yield is a miserly 0.5%. The S&P 500 index (^GSPC +1.60%) yields a bit over 1%, and the average pharmaceutical stock yields 1.3%. Again, you aren't getting any bargains when you buy Eli Lilly. And given the lofty valuation, if anything goes wrong, there's a material risk that mercurial investors move on to other stocks. That could result in a material decline in Eli Lilly's stock price rather than a continued upward climb.

    It has been revealed that so how likely is it that Eli Lilly stumbles? It is difficult to answer that question, but the risks are material. Yes, the manufacturer has done an excellent job with its GLP-1 drugs, and that's impressive. But drug patents eventually expire, so by design, this success comes with an expiration date. Which is why the healthcare giant's GLP-1 success is both good and bad.

    NYSE · As of 1:01 PM ET 11/27/26.

    The bad is twofold, with patent expirations merely setting up the larger problem. While the company's GLP-1 drug revenues are still growing rapidly, the company's weight-loss portfolio now accounts for more than 66% of its revenues. Eventually, Wall Street will start to worry about the size of the patent cliff Eli Lilly faces.

    To the company's credit, it is using its GLP-1 success to fund acquisitions that are expanding its portfolio into new treatment areas. So it is building a pipeline that may be able to offset the revenue hit that is on the way. However, there's no guarantee of success in that endeavor. Exciting new drug candidates fail all the time.

    Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, Eli Lilly isn't guaranteed to remain the GLP-1 kingpin it is today. Novo Nordisk (NVO +0.24%) has seen material success with its GLP-1 pill, and other companies, including industry giant Pfizer (PFE +0.21%), are hard at work on their own GLP-1 offerings. The competition in the GLP-1 space is going to be intense. The weight-loss market is likely to be huge, so there's room for more than one competitor. But Eli Lilly's current dominance may not last, even though continued dominance is likely being priced into its stock.

    Nobody knows what the future holds on Wall Street, so it is entirely possible that Eli Lilly's stock continues its ascent. But given the stock's valuation, the nature of the drug industry, and the manufacturer's current reliance on GLP-1 revenue, investors should probably adopt a cautious stance here.

    It has been revealed that wendy's carries risks including intense competition in the quick-service restaurant industry and reliance on the operational success of a predominantly franchised model.     By John Ballard – Nov 27, 2026 at 7:09PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

    In a recent development, anthropic (ANT +10.98%), the manufacturer behind the Claude family of artificial intelligence (AI) models, is officially a public company. Its shares, priced at $83 on Nov. 18, began trading the next day and closed trading on Friday, Nov. 20, at $88.91.

    NASDAQ · As of 1:15 PM ET 11/27/26.

    Sources indicate that many investors view Anthropic as a chatbot company charging everyone a similar monthly fee. However, its IPO filing tells a different story. Some business customers spend roughly 20 times as much as others, and the gap comes down to how they use the product. That difference may be the best clue to where Anthropic's next growth will come from.

    Claude Enterprise is the initiative Anthropic sells to businesses. It includes Claude.ai, the manufacturer's chat assistant, where you ask a question and get an answer.

    The bigger opportunity for Anthropic is to grow usage of its agentic AI models, such as Claude Code. This is Anthropic's coding agent, an AI that takes on a multistep task and carries it out. Anthropic calls it the product "we believe has most concretely defined what autonomous work at the frontier looks like.".

    In a recent development, in the three months ended Sept. 30, 2026, Claude Enterprise users who didn't use Claude Code spent less than $75 per month on average. The top 5% of Enterprise users who used Code spent about 20 times that amount.

    That matters because most of Anthropic's revenue is based on usage, rather than subscription fees. When a customer switches from chatting to doing agentic work with Code, the bill grows without Anthropic having to win a new customer. The firm says clients often start with one use case, then spread Claude across more departments. That's a growth engine that can compound for years.

    Anthropic has no public track record yet, and it's still losing money. It also competes with Alphabet's Google and OpenAI, and its filing says many rivals have greater resources. If one of them offered an equally good coding agent at a lower price, customers could shift work elsewhere, slowing the spending growth that supports the stock's price.

    It has been revealed that still, Anthropic's operating loss shrank in the first nine months of 2026 compared to a year earlier. Customers who hand Claude real work keep finding more for it to do. The growth from agentic models could be explosive.

    It has been revealed that the stock is more reasonably priced than its roughly $1.2 trillion market cap suggests. At Nov. 20’s price, it trades for about 14 times its run rate revenue, the company's measure of what its current sales would add up to over a full year. That looks expensive, but it's not considering how fast it is growing. Anthropic's annualized revenue jumped from $5 billion in August 2025 to $81 billion by Oct. 31, 2026.

    That is extraordinary. Enterprise spending could multiply rapidly as Claude's agentic AI models take on more work, allowing revenue to grow faster than the customer count.

    In a recent development, I believe that makes Anthropic worth a starter position today, with more added on dips. As long as usage keeps climbing and its operating loss narrows toward profitability, I'm interested in holding shares.

    10 stocks we like better than Monte Rosa Therapeutics ›.

    Industry observers note that monte Rosa Therapeutics (GLUE -3.85%) is going to the investor well again for fresh financing, and Mr. Market wasn't happy about it. That feeling translated into a sell-off on Friday that pushed the manufacturer's share price down by almost 4%.

    In a pair of regulatory filings, Monte Rosa disclosed that it is switching the underwriters assisting it in raising funds through share issues. It terminated its relationship with Jefferies (JEF +1.24%) and is now collaborating with TD Securities USA.

    Pursuant to that, Monte Rosa announced an at-the-market secondary stock offering of up to $100 million worth of its common stock.

    According to recent reports, as is typical with such arrangements, the tech giant will sell this equity from time to time through various means, including public offerings and private transactions. TD Securities USA will be paid up to 3% of the gross proceeds of such sales.

    Monte Rosa remarked it will use the raised funds to finance research and clinical development of its experimental drugs, capital expenditures, working capital, and for "general corporate purposes.".

    NASDAQ · As of 1:00 PM ET 11/27/26.

    It has been revealed that monte Rosa, which develops drugs called molecular glue degraders to treat a variety of disorders, raised $23.9 million in net proceeds under the arrangement with Jefferies. Investors were surely dismayed that the new relationship could potentially be more than four times that size and lead to significant dilution -- the tech giant's market cap is $767 million at present.

    While it’s not unusual for clinical-stage biotechs to tap investors for fresh financing, some are probably concerned that Monte Rosa has lately made a habit of it; meanwhile, it had over $578 million in cash and short-term investments on its books at the end of September. I think it'll have to demonstrate meaningful progress in at least one of its investigational programs to win back investors' hearts.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • I was unfashionably late to Nvidia (NVDA +0.80%) as an investor.
    • It has been revealed that with a cost basis in the high $170s, I was doing pretty well through the first few months.
    • I may as well start by addressing the situation with CEO Jensen Huang.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Rick Munarriz – Nov 27, 2026 at 7:38PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    I was unfashionably late to Nvidia (NVDA +0.80%) as an investor. These days, I'm unfortunately underwater. I've admired the business for decades, but it's only been eight months since I initiated a stake in the AI bellwether.

    It has been revealed that with a cost basis in the high $170s, I was doing pretty well through the first few months. The past month has been understandably rough. However, as I size up any portfolio moves I may want to make before heading into 2027, adding to my Nvidia position is on my short list. Let's go over some of the reasons I would be comfortable with buying more Nvidia in December.

    I may as well start by addressing the situation with CEO Jensen Huang. Nvidia stock was already under selling pressure before reports surfaced on not just one -- but two -- extramarital affairs. Failing the moral compass test comes with a reputational hit, but it's not necessarily a career killer. Presidents, coaches, and celebrities of all genders who get caught cheating don't automatically lose their high-profile positions.

    Both of Huang's adulterous accusations were problematic. Sleeping with an alleged Chinese spy posed a potential national security risk. Having a fling with a direct subordinate is reportedly against Nvidia's own code of ethics. You can't blame Nvidia directors for not simply sweeping it under the boardroom rug.

    Sources indicate that letting Huang go wasn't a surprise. Even founder CEOs aren't above a company's code of ethics. Huang hoping for a second chance and the board initially sticking to its druthers were the next obvious chess moves. Things get thorny here because of the political intervention. The White House boasting about pressuring Nvidia's board to take him back isn't going to pass a lot of sniff tests for overreach, but take a step back.

    Is the bigger risk here that Nvidia's board is now exposed as toothless, or what a hungry Huang could have done if he started a rival company? Nvidia directors will be fine in the aftermath. This isn't the kind of card a dismissed CEO can play twice, especially now with more eyes on him in social circles. The biggest positive of this very negative situation is that Nvidia and its moat are back at full strength.

    NASDAQ · As of 1:15 PM ET 11/27/26.

    A blowout report following a series of downticks is often the elixir that can turn a laggard into a leader. It didn't happen this time. Nvidia exceeded expectations. It boosted guidance for the next fiscal year. It wasn't enough to snap the bearish momentum.

    Nvidia and its interim CEO signaled that its prospects were getting brighter. The market still reached for the dimmer.

    I can very well be wrong, but looking back, this could be one of those obvious buying opportunities. A market that punishes improving fundamentals for a business that investors were already rotating out of doesn't typically stay down for long.

    Nvidia's revenue more than doubled in the quarter it reported 10 days ago. It's now modeling a 91% jump for the current quarter. It boosted its revenue growth outlook for the latest fiscal year starting in February from 70% to 75%.

    Sources indicate that you would expect to pay a healthy premium for this kind of growth. Instead, you can grab a piece of Nvidia for just 16 times trailing earnings and less than 9 times next year's profit target.

    In a recent development, let's reposition the cameras for a different shot of the same picture. Nvidia stock is down over the past week, even after Monday's historic but short-lived bounce. The shares have plummeted nearly 30% over the past month.

    In the past month, we've seen Nvidia's fiscal 2028 per-share profit target rise from $15.91 to $16.61. It's now expected to grow revenue and earnings by more than 70% next year. Last week it delivered its biggest earnings beat in more than a year.

    In a recent development, A lot can go wrong. The fast but now vulnerable wheels of the AI trade can get wobbly. Nvidia's record margins can contract. The floor might seem a lot lower than the ceiling may seem higher, but can you honestly feel that way given today's valuation? I believe Nvidia will beat the market from here, making it a rising name on my list of potential stocks to buy in December.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 27, 2026 at 7:46PM EST.
    • As digital transformation and artificial intelligence redefine corporate operations and personal finance, choosing between service giant Accenture (ACN +0.56%) and software leader Intuit (INTU +0.08%) represents a fundamental choice for investors.
    • Accenture focuses on global enterprise consulting and technology implementation, while Intuit dominates the tax and accounting software market for individuals and small businesses.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 27, 2026 at 7:46PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Accenture Plc ›.

    As digital transformation and artificial intelligence redefine corporate operations and personal finance, choosing between service giant Accenture (ACN +0.56%) and software leader Intuit (INTU +0.08%) represents a fundamental choice for investors.

    Accenture focuses on global enterprise consulting and technology implementation, while Intuit dominates the tax and accounting software market for individuals and small businesses. Both companies leverage massive data sets to improve their platforms, but they operate with different growth profiles and capital structures.

    Sources indicate that accenture serves approximately 9,000 clients, including about 75% of the Fortune Global 100 and 500 companies. This broad reach across the tech stocks landscape is supported by 18 key technology ecosystem partners that generate around 65% of its total revenue. The tech giant maintains deep roots with its clients, as 85% of its top 200 commercial partners have worked with the firm for 20 years or more.

    Industry observers note that in the 12 months ended Aug. 31, 2026, Accenture reported revenue of about $74.2 billion, representing 6.5% growth compared to the prior year. The organization delivered GAAP net income of approximately $8.4 billion during this period. This steady growth reflects a consistent demand for digital transformation services across its five major industry groups, including communications and financial services.

    Sources indicate that accenture maintains a debt-to-equity ratio of about 0.4x, which compares its total debt to shareholder equity. As of its August 2026 balance sheet, the current ratio is approximately 1.4x, indicating it can cover short-term liabilities with short-term assets. In the fiscal year ended Aug. 31, 2026, free cash flow was about $11.6 billion, representing the cash left after capital investments.

    Intuit serves about 93 million customers through its integrated financial technology platform, which includes household names like TurboTax and QuickBooks. The organization provides essential tools for tax preparation, small business accounting, and credit monitoring to a global user base. Its strategy focuses on an AI-driven ecosystem that automates business workflows and financial management for consumers and mid-market enterprises.

    In the 12 months ended Oct. 31, 2026, Intuit achieved revenue of about $21.9 billion, which marked a 12.8% increase over the previous year. The firm generated GAAP net income of approximately $4.8 billion during this same period. These results highlight the performance of its financial technology ecosystem, particularly as it expands into larger enterprise markets while maintaining its core consumer base.

    Industry observers note that intuit reported a debt-to-equity ratio of about 0.4x, while free cash flow reached about $8.7 billion in the fiscal year ended July 31, 2026. As of its July 2026 balance sheet, the current ratio of approximately 1.5x suggests it can meet short-term obligations. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 23.3% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

    Accenture faces intense competition from global technology providers like Amazon (AMZN +3.96%), offshore IT firms, and specialized consultancies. The company also manages significant cybersecurity risks, as sophisticated attacks targeting sensitive client data could damage its reputation and financial standing. Additionally, uncertain economic conditions may lead clients to reduce or defer spending on major digital projects.

    Intuit faces aggressive competition from both established entities and emerging start-ups, including potential government-funded tax software alternatives. The company also relies on third-party relationships with financial institutions and digital platform stores like those operated by Apple (AAPL +0.83%). Disruptions in these partnerships or shifts in generative AI accuracy could harm operations and customer trust.

    Accenture offers a lower P/S ratio, measuring price against sales over the past twelve months, while Intuit features a lower Forward P/E using future earnings estimates.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    I'd go with Intuit. Millions of people and small businesses count on its software every day for taxes and bookkeeping, from TurboTax to QuickBooks, and Intuit has built AI into those tools to handle chores like payroll, paying bills, and sending invoices. What impresses me is the momentum: Sales rose 12% year over year in its latest quarter, and customers can already use QuickBooks right inside popular AI chatbots.

    Intuit does have things to work through, though. Its growth is expected to slow to about 8% to 9% this fiscal year. Even so, its AI push gives it room to keep growing.

    In a recent development, to be fair to Accenture, it's a giant at helping companies put AI to work, and it returns lots of cash to shareholders. But analysts keep asking whether AI will let clients pay for fewer consulting hours, and Accenture indicates prices fell in many areas last quarter. Only about 3% of last year's 5% growth came from its own business, and it expects just 3% to 6% growth in the year ahead.

    Intuit, meanwhile, is growing faster and turning that growth into even bigger profit gains. For long-term investors, a software leader with momentum like this makes Intuit the better buy for 2027.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge.
    • Recent findings suggest that if Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113.
    • Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    As Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge. Unfortunately, they may have to wait until Monday, when options on the AI giant are expected to list.

    Recent findings suggest that if Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113. The wild price swings offer clues on how expensive it might be to buy protection on the upcoming tech giant once options begin trading.A 20% intraday move points to an implied volatility somewhere between 100 and 150 for Anthropic options, according to estimates from single-stock market-makers on the Cboe trading floor in Chicago.

    Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    Sources indicate that implied volatility in SpaceX started at 116, but that didn't deter options traders massive and small from piling into the contracts tracking the stock, with about 1.7 million contracts traded on the first day for a total options premium of about $2.5 billion. Far out-of-the-money call contracts were some of the most popular trades as the stock soared 40% in its first three sessions.One key difference between now and then? Anthropic is trading against the backdrop of S&P 500 volatility close to 30, compared to 17.3 when SpaceX debuted. "I expect ANT options to be super active," mentioned Tom Sosnoff, co-founder of the trading platforms ThinkOrSwim and TastyTrade. "I expect heavy options volume."One thing Anthropic and SpaceX have in common is heavy retail involvement in both IPOs, with retail brokerages receiving a 20% allocation from SpaceX and reports pointing to between a 15-20% allocation from Anthropic on Thursday. "Round one of the Anthropic IPO easily goes to the individual investor," Sosnoff added. "Retail participants bailed early at the best prices of the day while institutional investors paid up to top off their underwhelming allocations. I believe retail was aggressively reloading in the mid-90s."Further signs of retail demand will become evident when options likely begin trading on Monday. One thing to watch: the spread between out-of-the-money call and put contracts, which was heavily skewed toward calls in the case of SpaceX. "I would be careful comparing Anthropic to SpaceX," said Dennis Davitt, CIO and Co-Founder of Millbank Dartmoor Portsmouth. "From a market-structure perspective, the two are dramatically different. The availability and cost of borrowing will be different, the companies are at very different stages of maturity, and SpaceX has allowed employees to monetize portions of their holdings over time. All of those factors matter when pricing options.".

    • Recent findings suggest that A major part of the Vanguard Morningstar Growth ETF (VUG +2.06%) comes down to three companies.
    • And the past seven weeks have been tough for the fund.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 27, 2026 at 7:49PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Vanguard Morningstar Growth ETF ›.

    Recent findings suggest that A major part of the Vanguard Morningstar Growth ETF (VUG +2.06%) comes down to three companies. At the end of October, Apple (AAPL +0.83%) made up 13.7% of the fund's assets, Nvidia (NVDA +0.80%) 12.8%, and Microsoft (MSFT +0.60%) 10.5%. Together, they were around 37% of a fund that owns over 130 stocks.

    And the past seven weeks have been tough for the fund. Its record close was on Oct. 6, at $92.64. By Nov. 25, it had lost around 15%, to $79.10. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite has also slid around 15% from its Oct. 6 high. The S&P 500 is down around 8% over the same stretch.

    According to recent reports, but the fund's three giants haven't fallen together. Apple is the only one of them that's climbed since Oct. 6. Its stock has gained around 7% over that time, closing Nov. 25 at $355.58, within a dollar of its Nov. 13 record.

    Microsoft has dipped around 7%, a milder fall than the fund's.

    Nvidia, meanwhile, has plunged about 38%.

    Nvidia's slump started in October. Shares were down around 15% from their record by Oct. 30, and dropped further after Nvidia confirmed Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO on Nov. 12.

    Recent findings suggest that nvidia announced his reinstatement on Nov. 23. Still, Nvidia closed Nov. 25 at $149.30, well below its $239.24 record on Oct. 6.

    According to recent reports, but the chipmaker's sales are still booming. For Nvidia's fiscal third quarter of 2027, which ended Oct. 25, 2026, revenue grew 103% year over year to $115.8 billion. That was also a gain of 20% from the quarter before. And management guided for around $130 billion in sales for the fiscal fourth quarter, which includes an extra week.

    Microsoft's stock hit a record on Nov. 4, closing at $555.80, and it finished Nov. 25 around 12% under that peak. But in the software giant's first quarter of fiscal 2027 (the period ended Sept. 30, 2026), revenue climbed 19% to $92.3 billion, and revenue from its Azure cloud platform surged 48%.

    Sources indicate that apple's latest numbers were solid, too. Revenue in its fiscal fourth quarter of 2026, which ended Sept. 26, rose 12% year over year to $114.5 billion, a record for a September quarter. iPhone revenue grew 17% to $57.6 billion, and services revenue hit an all-time high of $31.6 billion.

    NASDAQ · As of 1:00 PM ET 11/27/26.

    The iPhone maker's growth, though, is cooling. For the June quarter (Apple's fiscal third quarter), revenue rose 16%. Then growth eased to 12% in the September quarter. This leaves Apple the slowest grower of the three, trailing Microsoft's 19% and Nvidia's 103%.

    On the earnings call, CFO Kevan Parekh guided for revenue growth of 7% to 10% for the December quarter. He noted the outlook reflects the manufacturer's best view of tight supply. By his account, then, the limit is supply, not demand.

    He also expects gross margin to be between 45% and 46%, and he pointed mostly to higher memory costs. That compares with 47.9% for the September quarter, which included about a percentage point of lift from tariff refunds.

    "What we're seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented," CEO John Ternus mentioned during the call.

    The fund owns every stock in around the same proportion as its weighting in the index it tracks, and these weights mostly shift with share prices. It doesn't sell what held up to buy more of what dropped.

    NYSEMKT · As of 1:00 PM ET 11/27/26.

    By my rough math, using Nov. 25 closing prices, Apple's weight has probably risen to around 15%, while Microsoft stands near 11% and Nvidia near 10%. The three still add up to more than a third of the fund. But the fund now leans harder on Apple than it did at the end of October.

    Recent findings suggest that this matters because Apple is also the priciest of the three. Its stock sells for around 40 times earnings, compared with about 16 times earnings for Nvidia. In other words, investors pay about two and a half times as much for every dollar of Apple's profit.

    Industry observers note that to the manufacturer's credit, Apple's revenue reached a record $479 billion for fiscal 2026, and its iPhone sales are still rising. But for those holding the fund into 2027, I think the bigger risk now is with Apple, not Nvidia. If Apple's growth keeps slowing while its memory costs rise, a stock at 40 times earnings might have room to fall. And the fund has more of it than it did in October.

    • Let's explore how much a $10,000 investment in Nvidia stock today could be worth by the end of 2027.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adam Spatacco – Nov 27, 2026 at 7:51PM EST.

    On Nov. 23, Nvidia (NVDA +0.80%) revealed that co-founder Jensen Huang had been reinstated as the organization's chief executive officer. Although Nvidia stock initially soared following the announcement, shares have subsequently surrendered some of those gains and remain approximately 38% below their all-time high from October.

    Interestingly, Nvidia's recent sell-off comes at a time when the company's financial outlook is becoming even more encouraging. Between accelerating revenue and earnings growth, an enormous share repurchase program, and a historically inexpensive valuation, Nvidia looks positioned for an incredible comeback.

    Let's explore how much a $10,000 investment in Nvidia stock today could be worth by the end of 2027.

    Industry observers note that during the third quarter of fiscal 2027 (ended Oct. 25), Nvidia generated $115.8 billion in revenue, representing 103% growth year over year. Meanwhile, adjusted earnings per share (EPS) increased by 111% to $2.68. Moreover, management raised its fiscal 2028 revenue guidance from 70% to 75%.

    Assuming Nvidia meets its fourth-quarter revenue outlook of $130 billion, the tech giant should finish fiscal 2027 with roughly $424 billion in sales. This implies revenue approaching $742 billion next year.

    Industry observers note that while Nvidia continues to benefit from robust demand for its Blackwell chip architecture, the commercialization of its Vera Rubin architecture has become the company's next major growth catalyst. Nvidia's latest computing platform incorporates graphics processing units (GPUs), Vera central processing units (CPUs), and advanced networking technologies.

    Industry observers note that this combination broadens Nvidia's opportunities to monetize different layers of the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure value chain. As hyperscalers continue investing in data center expansion, Nvidia's comprehensive product portfolio provides the tech giant with multiple avenues to sustain its growth.

    NASDAQ · As of 1:15 PM ET 11/27/26.

    Industry observers note that in September, Nvidia's board of directors increased the tech giant's share repurchase authorization by $150 billion. As of the end of October, Nvidia had $227.3 billion remaining under its buyback program. Management intends to execute the buybacks by the end of fiscal 2028.

    Sources indicate that interestingly, Nvidia's recent share-price depreciation could make these repurchases more accretive to shareholders. Even if net income remained flat, reducing the outstanding share count should increase Nvidia's EPS considerably.

    Over the last five years, Nvidia has traded at an average forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of approximately 32. Following its recent sell-off, Nvidia is trading at roughly 8.9 times estimated earnings over the next 12 months.

    In a recent development, given Nvidia's enormous size, I don't expect the organization to reclaim its historical average valuation profile. However, even modest multiple expansion could generate multibagger returns.

    It has been revealed that by the end of next year, investors will be valuing Nvidia based on its fiscal 2029 earnings potential. Presently, Wall Street expects Nvidia to generate normalized EPS of approximately $21.65 in fiscal 2029. Applying a forward P/E multiple of 15 to this earnings estimate implies a stock price of roughly $325.

    NVDA EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts.

    Recent findings suggest that using Nvidia's recent share price of $149, a $325 price target implies 118% upside. This would transform a $10,000 investment into roughly $21,800 in just one year.

    Given Nvidia's accelerating earnings potential and historically compressed valuation, the firm's recent sell-off could represent a lucrative opportunity to buy the dip for patient investors.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Two Italians have been killed after an alleged Iranian attack on Kuwait, Kuwaiti forces remarked Thursday.
    • In a post on X, Kuwait's army stated the deaths followed Iranian attacks on the country, with the two Italians killed by falling missile debris.
    • Sources indicate that in response, a spokesperson for Iran's military told state media that no offensive or military operations had been carried out in the area and that "these accusations should be viewed as a cover for continued malevolence and an attempt to exacerbate insecurity in the region" by U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Two Italians have been killed after an alleged Iranian attack on Kuwait, Kuwaiti forces remarked Thursday.

    In a post on X, Kuwait's army stated the deaths followed Iranian attacks on the country, with the two Italians killed by falling missile debris. Two others were also injured.

    Sources indicate that in response, a spokesperson for Iran's military told state media that no offensive or military operations had been carried out in the area and that "these accusations should be viewed as a cover for continued malevolence and an attempt to exacerbate insecurity in the region" by U.S. and Israeli forces.

    Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated on Telegram that he had spoken with his Italian counterpart, Antonio Tajani, and expressed regret over their deaths, while stressing that Tehran had no role or involvement in the incident.

    "The incident is suspicious and looks like a precooked recipe for war," Araghchi wrote on X.

    He also said Iran was ready to cooperate with the governments of Kuwait and Italy in investigating the incident.

    Recent findings suggest that separately, Israel stated Thursday that it was prepared to carry out strikes against Iran "at any moment," even without U.S. forces joining the effort, according to Israeli military spokesman Effie Defrin on Israeli broadcaster Kan.

    The comments came after U.S. envoy Jared Kushner told a podcast Wednesday that Israel "needs to get out of the constant wartime mindset.".

    It has been revealed that israel has been pushing the Trump administration to back another offensive against Tehran, with Reuters reporting on Nov. 18 that Israeli spy chief Roman Gofman pushed for joint strikes when he met U.S. officials earlier in the month.

    Late Thursday, President Donald Trump noted on PBS that the U.S. had "victory at hand" in the Iran conflict and reiterated that victory would come "whenever I want it to be, to be honest.".

    Speaking during a Thanksgiving call with U.S. military personnel, Trump said Washington was still trying to give Iran "every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives.".

    But he added that he was not sure whether Tehran would agree.

    "Some people question why. Are they crazy? Maybe they are," Trump stated.

    "They just don't make things like they used to." The phrase, formerly exclusive to grandparents, is now used by consumers of all ages.

    Sources indicate that across the United States, durable goods like cars, appliances and electronics are becoming less reliable. In the automobile industry, owners of 3-year-old models reported an average of 204 problems per 100 vehicles as of Feb. 12, the highest level since 2022, according to a report from consumer intelligence organization J.D. Power. Reliability is a growing concern for dishwashers and front-load washers too, respectively experiencing an average of 92 and 91 problems per 100 units as of Oct. 29, according to a similar J.D. Power report.

    Industry observers note that consumers have noticed: Shoppers dealing with high inflation rates and added tariffs on imported goods are unsatisfied with all kinds of products, from cars and tech devices to furniture and kitchen gear. Just over three-quarters of Americans say they believe companies often sell lower-quality products and services at higher prices, according to an Axios and Harris Poll survey published in May 2025.

    Recent findings suggest that to be sure, reliability and durability aren't the only ways to define a product's quality. Aesthetics and performance matter to consumers, too. Your television today may not last as long as the one you grew up with, but it's probably larger and thinner with better picture definition — and it likely costs much less, when adjusted for inflation, says Justin Sirotin, an industrial design professor at the Rhode Island School of Design. Indeed, the average price of a television was roughly $622 in 1996 adjusted for inflation, whereas a 55-inch LCD model now costs $232 on average.

    But because they're penny-pinched, consumers are becoming more focused on finding high-value products — ones that perform consistently and reliably — than on price, according to a 2025 Deloitte report.

    Sources indicate that unfortunately for shoppers, some businesses are also economically squeezed, and may manufacture products with cheaper, less durable parts to keep their profits growing, Sirotin says. Plus, we've all gotten used to sleek products with impressive features at affordable prices, and when businesses have to deliver on those aspects to grow demand, longevity can drop down the list of priorities. Manufacturers may prioritize quality on the external parts of a product — like the picture quality on a television — and get their cost savings with cheaper internal components that you won't initially notice, says Keyana Sapp, an investigative journalist and creator of the Worse on Purpose newsletter.

    According to recent reports, in some cases, a product's durability may even be part of a "planned obsolescence," wherein businesses intentionally give goods a certain lifespan so customers need to buy replacements within a predictable timeframe. Planned obsolescence isn't necessarily rampant, and it's hard to prove that any individual company purposefully designs products to fail, Sapp states.

    Sources indicate that but historically speaking, it's not entirely a conspiracy theory. In 1924, major light bulb manufacturers formed an international coalition and agreed to lower and standardize the lifespan of incandescent light bulbs to 1,000 hours. The cartel broke up during World War II.

    According to recent reports, you can, of course, try extending the longevity of products you've already bought by paying to repair them, rather than getting a brand-new replacement. But as devices like vacuum cleaners and headphones evolve technologically, they require increasingly specialized tools and labor, claims Shahram Mokhtari, lead teardown technician at online repair community and e-commerce site iFixit. Specialized screws, glued components and limited access to repair information can make some products difficult or impossible to fix, the Federal Trade Commission reported in May 2021.

    Europe has right-to-repair regulations that require manufacturers of certain products to provide access to replacement parts, tools and information. Only nine U.S. states have similar legislation for consumer electronics.

    According to recent reports, if you want to know how long a product might last before you buy it, look up its reviews or do some research to understand if it's complicated to fix, Mokhtari recommends. Or, if you have the budget, you can prioritize higher-priced products that might bring both initial quality and long-term longevity. This may require intentional long-term planning for some consumers — even as online shopping has made impulse buying easier, Sirotin notes.

    "It takes a lot of intentionality by the consumer to say, 'OK, well, is this chair really a chair that I want to have for 25 years? Or is this the chair I'm going to buy and sit in for six months, and then I'm just going to get another chair?'" claims Sirotin.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.
    • In a recent development, on platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026.
    • Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.

    In a recent development, on platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026. On Oct. 13, those odds were as high as 72%.

    Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.

    On Friday, the Nasdaq Composite turned negative for the year as investors continued to dump tech stocks, primarily those with exposure to the artificial intelligence build-out. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 fell into correction territory, too.

    The S&P 500 has slashed its year-to-date gain to just over 2%.

    The Stock Trader's Almanac in a Thursday note broadly agreed that the hopes for a December rally are fading, with the caveat that a "Santa rally" could still appear at the end of the year.

    "The market is under pressure and more downside can't be ruled out," the note stated.

    The Stock Trader's Almanac sees 2026 following the year-end pattern of 2018, when the Federal Reserve was in a tightening cycle in a midterm year. The Fed is widely expected to hike rates at its December meeting.

    According to recent reports, in that scenario, the Stock Trader's Almanac thinks more churn is to come. "The low is more likely in mid- to late December than this week.".

    Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    When Shane Beatty, a contestant on NBC's "The Traitors: Latest Blood," deceived his fellow finalists, he walked away with the entire $246,300 prize. But the emotional toll of winning caught him by surprise.

    Sources indicate that "The second I had to reveal that I was a Traitor, everything hit me at once," Beatty, a 32-year-old ironworker from Staten Island, Fresh York, tells CNBC Make It. "I had built genuine relationships with these people, and knowing that some of them were blindsided by my decision was difficult.".

    According to recent reports, now that he's won, Beatty has a proposal for his money, starting with setting aside a sizable share for Uncle Sam. As for the rest, he's more interested in financial security than the trappings of newfound wealth.

    After winning, Beatty doesn't expect his day-to-day life to change much.

    According to recent reports, "I'm still going to get up, go to work, and continue doing what I've been doing as a Local 580 ironworker," he states. "I love my career, and winning this money doesn't change that.".

    Beatty prepares to pay for a wedding he and his fiancée previously struggled to afford, help his mother pay down debt and clear his own debts before saving the rest.

    "What it does give me is an opportunity to take some financial pressure off, be a little more comfortable and put myself in a better position for the future," he says.

    But before spending his winnings, Beatty is accounting for what could be his single biggest expense — taxes.

    "First thing I'm gonna do with the money is put at least $100,000 in a separate bank account just so I can have it ready for Uncle Sam," he told Entertainment Weekly last week.

    Setting aside $100,000 is a reasonable move given Beatty's potential tax liability, according to tax experts.

    It has been revealed that "Taxes are often an afterthought when winning big on a gameshow," states Riley Adams, a certified public accountant and founder of Sequoia Ridge CPAs. "So, it's definitely smart on his part to get ahead with his tax planning.".

    Game show winnings are generally taxed as ordinary income, meaning the prize money is added to a winner's other taxable income for the year. That can push a winner into higher tax brackets.

    In addition to federal income taxes, Beatty, who lives in Upcoming Jersey, will have to account for state income taxes.

    While Beatty did not disclose his income to CNBC Make It, ironworkers in the New York City metropolitan area typically earn around $100,000 a year, according to 2025 Bureau of Labor Statistics data.

    Assuming Beatty lives in Newly introduced Jersey, earns $100,000 from his job in New York in 2026, receives his winnings this year, files as a single taxpayer with no dependents and takes the standard deduction, here's how much of his prize money he could keep, according to Adams' calculations:.

    Under this scenario, Beatty's winnings would push him from the 22% federal income tax bracket into the 35% bracket. Factoring in state income taxes, an estimated 35% of his prize would go to taxes, according to Adams' calculations. Setting aside $100,000 would give Beatty a comfortable cushion under this scenario. His actual tax bill, however, will depend on his income, deductions and other financial circumstances.

    Jim Guarino, a certified public accountant and managing director at Baker Newman Noyes in Woburn, Massachusetts, arrived at a similar estimate.

    "Folks tend to get excited by the 'gross amount' of their total winnings," but Beatty is "extremely tax-aware" in recognizing how much less he'll actually get to keep after taxes, he notes.

    For Beatty, the money won't radically change his life, but it will give him greater financial security.

    "Having a savings cushion and knowing I don't have to worry about living paycheck to paycheck or falling behind on bills means so much to me," he indicates. "I want to be responsible with this opportunity and make sure it gives me greater financial peace of mind.".

    #166568. The Tech Download: Will Jensen Huang’s return be the spark the shaky AI market needs?

    📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (641 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    The Tech Download: Will Jensen Huang’s return be the spark the shaky AI market needs?

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (641 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The recent Nvidia saga has had more twists and turns than an Agatha Christie novel.
    • Recent findings suggest that it all started with Nvidia co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang's admission that he had been unfaithful to his wife.
    • During all of that, Nvidia stock lost over $1 trillion and then regained just under $1 trillion.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The recent Nvidia saga has had more twists and turns than an Agatha Christie novel.

    Recent findings suggest that it all started with Nvidia co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang's admission that he had been unfaithful to his wife. Days later, amid an independent board investigation and broader scrutiny over national-security concerns, he resigned. Less than two weeks later, Huang was back at the helm.

    During all of that, Nvidia stock lost over $1 trillion and then regained just under $1 trillion.

    The leadership drama has played out at a time when the artificial intelligence market is looking shakier than it has in some time.

    Neoclouds have seen stocks plummet in recent months as investors question the sustainability of the AI boom. Chip stocks like Arm and AMD have both fallen in the past month.

    Sources indicate that huang's surprise return saw Nvidia stock surge 31%, with other AI stocks also gaining. But the sheen was off by Tuesday's close, with Nvidia and a host of chip stocks falling.

    The sharp reversal raises questions for investors: did Huang's return restore confidence in Nvidia, or did it spark a short-lived relief rally as the market faces broader questions about returns on AI investment?

    Judging by the first few days of his return, it's a hard one to call.

    Volatility in the tech sector looked set to continue on Friday, as tech stocks rebounded again.

    "Wall Street pared its Monday advance as sobriety returned to the market and a focus returned to fundamentals," wrote Kyle Rodda, analyst at Capital.com, in a note at market close on Tuesday.

    "While Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO is indubitably a boon for the markets and the overall AI trade, it does not assuage every risk and concern about an industry confronting a potential peak in its investment boom and moderating earnings growth.".

    The early week rally was "largely driven" by Huang's return, mentioned Violeta Todorova, senior research analyst at Leverage Shares.

    "Fresh tariff threats from the Trump administration have added to market uncertainty," she added. "The short-term rally has reversed course, and Nvidia's share price is likely to trade sideways between $125 and $170 in the near term.".

    Nvidia stock closed at $149.30 on Wednesday, giving it a $3.6 trillion market cap — a figure around $2 trillion lighter than it was at its peak in October.

    "We expect a selective recovery across the AI ecosystem, and NVDA to trade sideways and stay volatile below its October peak at least until the Dec 1–3 Congressional appearances," Egor Tolmachev, senior analyst at Freedom Capital Markets, stated in a note on Wednesday.

    Other key AI stocks have also been volatile. Anthropic's first week as a public tech giant has been mixed. AMD has fallen 25% in the past five days, and memory chip maker Micron has dropped 18%. Both spiked on Monday before paring gains.

    The Huang evangelists might've been hoping for a speedier return to AI boom times.

    But while the Nvidia CEO's return has removed one source of uncertainty around the chip giant, the volatility among AI stocks suggests investors are still trading on questions much bigger than who occupies the chief executive's office.

    Tech German software major SAP is reportedly weighing cutting at least 10,000 jobs in AI push.

    According to recent reports, U.S. adds Megaspeed to trade blacklist over export control concerns amid Nvidia controversy.

    Robots could be doing household chores in just 1-2 years, a Chinese EV firm says.

    SpaceX, Musk pledge to donate a share each to active Trump Accounts.

    Jensen Huang tells staff that Nvidia doesn't need a succession initiative, according to people inside the room.

    Jensen Huang is back as the CEO of Nvidia, and is now tasked with selling the firm's AI vision while also defending himself in Washington, my colleague Kif Leswing wrote on Tuesday.
